title: DEV_CONSOLE_CMDS lists 5 commands the project does not register
body:
## Summary
The Debug tab's compact command list (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/data.ts:15) offers godmode, give, setlevel, spawn, killall; the UE project's cheat manager registers ARPGGod, ARPGSetLevel, ARPGGiveXP, ARPGKillAll, ARPGSpawnEnemy.

## Description
DEBUG_COMMANDS (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/data.ts:15-21) is rendered with a copy button per row (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/index.tsx:93-107). Pasting any of them into the UE console does nothing: the project's Exec UFUNCTIONs live in Source/PoF/Debug/ARPGCheatManager.h (ARPGGod, ARPGSetLevel(int32), ARPGGiveXP(float), ARPGHeal, ARPGKillAll, ARPGSpawnEnemy(path, level), ARPGDamageTarget, ARPGShowStats). 'give <id> <count>' has no counterpart at all. Fixed = the list names the registered Exec commands with their real signatures.

## Flow
- open Core Engine > Debug > Dashboard
- copy "godmode" from DEV_CONSOLE_CMDS
- paste into the UE console -> "Command not recognized"
- fix: rewrite DEBUG_COMMANDS from ARPGCheatManager.h and pin the names with a test fixture

## Expected impact
A developer using the panel gets working cheats instead of dead strings. Breaks nothing in-app; the names are display data.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every listed debug command exists in the project
Before: 0 of 5 listed names match a registered Exec (grep UFUNCTION(Exec) ARPGCheatManager.h: 8 exec functions, all ARPG-prefixed)
After: 5 of 5 expected once rewritten (not built: the truth lives in the UE repo, outside this tree)
Method: probe - grep of the UE header vs the list; no in-tree gate can read the UE repo
Result: better
Gate: contract
instrument: a fixture copied from ARPGCheatManager.h exec names + a test asserting every DEBUG_COMMANDS syntax head is in it

title: Triage failure drops the route reason
body:
## Summary
When the triage request fails, useDebugSnapshot maps it to triage=null and the queue says "Triage could not be run for <name>." with no reason (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/useDebugSnapshot.ts:88).

## Description
The triage branch is `.then((r) => (r.ok ? r.data.triage ?? null : null))` (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/useDebugSnapshot.ts:88): r.error is discarded, so the operator cannot tell a DB error from a missing session. The compare branch now carries compareError (commit 7f9f0b9b); triage should carry triageError the same way and OptimizationQueue.tsx:105 should print it.

## Flow
- newest capture exists, triage route returns {success:false,error}
- queue shows "Triage could not be run for X." with no cause
- fix: add triageError to LatestTriage.ready, render it

## Expected impact
The operator sees why triage failed. Risk: none beyond the note text.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a failed triage names its cause
Before: 0 of 1 triage failure reasons surfaced (r.error discarded at useDebugSnapshot.ts:88)
After: 1 of 1 predicted, same shape as compareError
Method: simulation - walked the failure path in code; the gate is a 20-line hook test not built for budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/useDebugSnapshot.ts:88 postProfiling<{ triage: TriageResult }>({ action: 'triage', ... }).then((r) => (r.ok ? r.data.triage ?? null : null))
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/performance/OptimizationQueue.tsx:105 else if (!latest.triage) body = <Note>Triage could not be run for {latest.session.name}.</Note>;
instrument: hook test: triage route returns {success:false,error:"x"} -> latest.triageError === "x" and the note contains it

title: useLatestTriage has no production consumer
body:
## Summary
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/useLatestTriage.ts is imported only by its own test; no component calls it.

## Description
The hook is a thin selector over useDebugSnapshot().latest. Its doc says the dashboard passes `latest` down and to use the hook "only from a surface that does not" - none exists. Worse, any future caller would instantiate a SECOND useDebugSnapshot reader (its own list + get-session + triage + compare requests), contradicting the "never a second fetch path" claim in its own doc. Remove it and point debug-latest-triage.test.tsx at useDebugSnapshot().latest; drop it from context-map file_paths.

## Flow
- grep useLatestTriage over src: 1 test file, 0 components
- delete the hook; retarget the test to useDebugSnapshot
- rescan context map

## Expected impact
One less file and one less trap that would double the profiler requests. Breaks nothing (0 consumers).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dead export removed
Before: 1 file, 0 production consumers
After: 0 files; test coverage kept via useDebugSnapshot
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
grep -rn "useLatestTriage" src --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx (excluding the file itself):
src/__tests__/components/core-engine/debug-latest-triage.test.tsx:3,60,63,72
(no other hits)
instrument: zero-consumer grep + the retargeted debug-latest-triage test green; context-map.json edit is director-owned

title: Command catalog rows and RUN are unreachable by keyboard
body:
## Summary
Each catalog row is a div with onClick (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/console/CommandCatalog.tsx:73) and its RUN button is opacity-0 until mouse hover, with no focus variant.

## Description
The row's populate action has no role, tabIndex or key handler, so a keyboard user cannot fill a command. The RUN/FILL button is in the tab order but rendered with `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` and nothing for focus (CommandCatalog.tsx:96), so it is invisible when focused. Fixed = row action is a real button (or role=button + Enter/Space), RUN gains `group-focus-within:opacity-100 focus-visible:opacity-100` and the shared .focus-ring.

## Flow
- Tab into the COMMAND CATALOG
- focus lands on an invisible RUN button; rows cannot be activated
- fix: button semantics + focus-visible opacity

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can use the catalog. Risk: layout of the row if it becomes a <button>.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - catalog operable by keyboard
Before: 0 of 12 rows keyboard-activatable; 12 of 12 RUN buttons invisible on focus
After: 12 of 12 predicted
Method: simulation - read the markup; a jsdom test can assert role/tabIndex and the focus class but not visibility
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/console/CommandCatalog.tsx:73 <div key={cmd.syntax} onClick={() => onPopulate(cmd.syntax)} className="... cursor-pointer ...">
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/console/CommandCatalog.tsx:96 className="... opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 disabled:opacity-30"
instrument: component test: each row exposes role=button + tabIndex=0 and Enter populates; RUN className contains a focus-visible opacity variant

title: FPS sparkline goes Infinity/NaN on a zero-length frame
body:
## Summary
projectStats builds the FPS sparkline as 1000 / f.totalFrameMs (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/debugSnapshot.ts:131) with no guard; one 0 ms frame in a CSV capture yields Infinity and the Sparkline polyline gets NaN points.

## Description
Sparkline (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/system/CircularGauge.tsx:105-118) computes min/max over the data; with an Infinity value range is Infinity and every y becomes NaN, so the whole line disappears. A CSV stats capture can contain a zero frame row (csv-parser has no lower clamp on totalFrameMs). Fix: skip or clamp non-finite points in the projection.

## Flow
- import a CSV with one 0 ms frame
- Stat dashboard > Frame > FPS sparkline renders nothing
- fix: filter Number.isFinite in the FPS series

## Expected impact
One bad frame no longer blanks the FPS trend. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - projection tolerates a zero frame
Before: 1 Infinity point -> 12 of 12 polyline points NaN (walked)
After: 0 NaN points predicted
Method: simulation - walked the arithmetic; reachability depends on csv-parser output, not proven on a real capture
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/debugSnapshot.ts:131 sparkline: series((f) => round1(1000 / f.totalFrameMs))
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/system/CircularGauge.tsx:108-110 const min = Math.min(...data); const max = Math.max(...data); const range = max - min || 1;
instrument: projection test: SAMPLE_SESSION with frameSamples[0].totalFrameMs = 0 -> every FPS sparkline value is finite

title: CSV captures fabricate GC timestamps, so the GC interval is invented
body:
## Summary
csv-parser stamps GC pauses at i * 5000 ms ("Approximate spacing", src/lib/profiling/csv-parser.ts:283); the Debug tab then shows "AVG: 5s" interval and a timeline as if measured (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/performance/GCTimelineSection.tsx:22).

## Description
projectGc derives avgIntervalS from timestampMs gaps (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/debugSnapshot.ts:126-131). For every CSV capture those gaps are exactly 5000 ms by construction, so the header always reads 5s and the bars are evenly spaced regardless of the real run. The tab's own rule is "absent, never invented" (NOT_IN_CAPTURE, debugSnapshot.ts:47). Fixed = the parser marks timestamps as synthetic (or omits them) and the tab shows interval n/a + an index axis for such sessions.

## Flow
- import any UE stats CSV with GC rows
- GC_TIMELINE header: AVG 5s, bars evenly spaced
- fix: flag synthetic timing in the session and project interval as null

## Expected impact
The GC panel stops presenting a made-up cadence as a measurement. Touches src/lib/profiling (out of this context).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no invented figure shown as measured
Before: CSV path: avgIntervalS == 5.0 for 100% of captures with >=2 GC rows (constant by construction)
After: n/a shown for synthetic timing
Method: probe - read csv-parser.ts:283 and the projection; constant follows arithmetically
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/profiling/csv-parser.ts:283 timestampMs: i * 5000, // Approximate spacing
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/debugSnapshot.ts:128 avgIntervalS: gaps.length > 0 ? round1(gaps.reduce(...) / gaps.length / 1000) : null
instrument: parser test: GC rows -> pauses flagged synthetic; projection test: synthetic -> avgIntervalS null (out-of-scope: profiling lib owner)

title: Memory "Peak" sums per-category peaks that never coincide
body:
## Summary
projectMemory reports peakMB = sum of every category's own peak (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/debugSnapshot.ts:115), shown as "Peak" in the memory panel and stat dashboard.

## Description
Category peaks occur at different times; their sum is an upper bound, not a peak the process reached. The same rule is duplicated in csv-parser.ts:308 and sample-generator.ts:208, so all three agree on an overstated figure. Fixed = either a true concurrent peak from per-frame totals when the capture has them, or the label says "Sum of category peaks".

## Flow
- open Debug > Memory
- Peak reads 412MB (sample) = 185+104+40+33+30+20
- fix: relabel or compute the concurrent peak

## Expected impact
Memory headroom decisions use an honest figure. Label-only fix is XS; true peak needs per-frame memory the capture may not hold.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - "Peak" names what it is
Before: 3 of 3 implementations sum category peaks under the label Peak
After: label matches the computation (1 of 1 surfaces)
Method: probe - read the three implementations
Result: better
Gate: direction
instrument: none needed for the label; the definition choice (relabel vs measure) is the operator's

title: Optimization queue forgets dispatched fixes on remount
body:
## Summary
OptimizationQueue keeps finding-id -> dispatch time in component useState (src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/performance/OptimizationQueue.tsx:94); a reload or LRU eviction resets every 'dispatched' row to 'open'.

## Description
The verification model (buildOptimizationQueue, src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/optimizationQueue.ts:63-72) needs the dispatch time to decide 'still-present' (a capture taken AFTER the dispatch). Losing it means a fix dispatched before a reload can never be shown as still-present, and the operator is offered "Fix" again as if nothing was tried. Fixed = persist dispatches (per session id) in a store or the profiling DB.

## Flow
- click Fix on a finding -> row shows dispatched
- reload the app
- row shows open; after re-capture it can never read still-present

## Expected impact
The verify-by-recapture loop survives navigation. Needs a persistence choice (store vs DB).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - dispatch state survives remount
Before: 0 of N dispatched rows survive a remount (useState only)
After: N of N predicted with persisted dispatches
Method: simulation - walked the state; a remount test would measure it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/performance/OptimizationQueue.tsx:94 const [dispatched, setDispatched] = useState<Record<string, number>>({});
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_debug/_shared/optimizationQueue.ts:70 return { finding, state: persisting.has(finding.id) && headAt > at ? 'still-present' : 'dispatched' };
instrument: component test: dispatch, unmount, remount -> row still dispatched
